title: Test Case: Ear Pain and Hearing Change
subtitle: For testing the case flow and answer records
coverDescription:
This is a test case for checking the post-login case entry, pre-test, clinical reasoning, and post-test flow.

Learning goal: Practice building an initial differential from ear pain and hearing change.

preTest.title: Pre-Test
preTest.instructions: Answer this test question before starting.

questions.text: When a patient has ear pain and hearing loss, what should be clarified first?

options.text: The timing and progression of symptoms

questions.explanation: Clarifying the symptom timeline helps establish the differential diagnosis.

slides.content: A 28-year-old patient presents with right ear pain and mild hearing loss that have lasted for two days.

slides.title: History Taking
slides.instruction: Organize the history that needs to be clarified.

questionsAndRationales.question: Is there fever, ear discharge, or recent swimming?
questionsAndRationales.rationale: This helps distinguish infection from an external ear canal problem.

steps.name: Auricle and Ear Canal
steps.description: Check the auricle and ear canal for swelling, discharge, and tenderness.

clinicalDecision.question: What should be done after the initial examination?
clinicalDecision.reasoning: Integrate the history and examination before deciding whether further testing is needed.
clinicalDecision.answer: Organize the history and examination findings

investigations.name: Pure Tone Audiometry
investigations.question: Should the hearing change be confirmed?
investigations.answer: Yes. Audiometry provides an objective assessment of hearing.

options.text: Arrange further assessment based on the history and examination.
options.feedback: Correct. The test case flow can continue.

options.text: End the assessment without taking a history.

interactive.instructions: Describe your initial clinical reasoning in one sentence.

questions.text: What information should be clarified first in this case?
questions.hint: Start with the symptom timeline and main symptoms.

feedbackTemplate.excellent: Complete answer. You identified the key points of this test case.
feedbackTemplate.good: Good direction. Add the symptom timeline.
feedbackTemplate.hint: Mention the ear pain, hearing change, and symptom timing.

postTest.title: Post-Test
postTest.instructions: Answer this test question after completing the case.

questions.text: What is the most reasonable next step after the case assessment?

options.text: Plan follow-up based on the history, examination, and test results
Do not record the assessment findings

questions.explanation: Clinical reasoning uses the complete set of findings to plan management.
